intro.text: In Chapter 1 you learned to move around the terminal. Now it's time to meet the tool that does the actual coding in this course: Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding agent that runs in that same terminal. As a manager, you won't write the code — Claude Code will — but you are the one who sets it up, points it at the work, and judges what comes back. In this chapter you'll learn what Claude Code is and why we chose it, create an Anthropic account and subscribe, install Claude Code on your own machine (Windows or macOS), and run it for the first time — ending with your very first AI-built website: delivered by the AI, inspected and accepted by you.

intro.title: Before you continue
intro.text: Lessons 2.3 and 2.4 cover the same installation on different operating systems — work through the one that matches your laptop.

lessons.title: Meet Claude Code
lessons.objective: Understand what Claude Code — the AI that will do the coding in this course — is, well enough to explain what it can do, justify why we chose it, and account for what it costs.

blocks.text: Claude Code is an AI coding agent that codes for you automatically, powered by Claude — Anthropic's large language model.

Describe the program you want in ordinary language. Claude Code can inspect files, propose or make edits, run commands with the applicable permissions, and help diagnose errors. You still review and test its work.
An AI program that goes beyond chatting — one that directly edits your files and carries out the work — is what we call an AI coding agent.

steps.title: How is it different from other agents?

blocks.text: There are plenty of coding agents out there — Google's Antigravity, and more. A manager should be able to defend a tooling choice, so here's why this course picked Claude Code:
Using the same coding agent gives everyone in this course a shared workflow for writing prompts, reviewing edits, and checking results.
We use Claude Code in the terminal. This makes it possible to describe the same workflow on Windows and Mac. Labels and features can still change between versions.
For this course, use Claude Code with your Claude Pro subscription. Sign in with that subscription account rather than selecting separate API billing.
Pro costs about $20 per month (about $17/month if you pay annually).
Choose monthly billing for the course. Start with one month of Pro, and cancel before the next billing date if you do not plan to continue using it.

lessons.title: Claude Code: Account and Subscription
lessons.objective: Create the Anthropic account you need for Claude Code, walk through subscribing to the Pro plan start to finish, and confirm on screen that the plan is actually active before any work begins.

blocks.text: Claude Code runs on Claude, the AI made by a company called Anthropic. So you need two things:
An Anthropic account — free
A Pro (or higher) subscription — about $20 per month
Create or sign in to your Claude account, then confirm the monthly plan and price before subscribing.
Create or sign in to your Claude account using the account setup section:
https://github.com/cyj-oss/itm325-setup#prepare-your-claude-account
Go to the pricing page
Click the account menu in the bottom-left corner, or the Upgrade button in the top-right.
Pro vs. Max
Anthropic offers two main paid plans:
Pro — about $20/month (about $17/month billed annually). Plenty for following this course.
Max — about $100–200/month. Much higher Claude Code usage limits, meant for working developers who code all day.
“If you're here for the course, start with one month of Pro.”
blocks.title: Another way to think about it

blocks.text: After the course activity, cancel if you will no longer use the subscription. To avoid another charge, cancel at least 24 hours before your next billing date. Your paid access continues until the end of the current billing period.
Enter payment details
Click the Subscribe button under Pro and you'll be taken to the payment page. Enter your card details and complete the payment.

blocks.title: Before you continue
blocks.text: If the charge doesn't go through, your bank may be flagging a new online subscription. Check your banking app for a declined-transaction alert, approve it, and try again.
Once payment finishes you're returned to the claude.ai main screen. If the account menu in the bottom-left now shows a Pro (or Max) label, everything worked.
When you install Claude Code in the next lesson, you'll log in with this account and start using it right away.

lessons.title: Claude Code Basics
lessons.objective: Run the Claude Code you just installed, get comfortable with the commands that let you direct and monitor it, and judge whether its first deliverable matches what you asked for.

steps.title: Before you run it: make a safe working folder

blocks.text: Use a dedicated course workspace. If the installation guide already created webdev, use that existing folder. Find it in File Explorer or Finder and confirm its actual location before starting Claude Code. Do not create a second webdev folder just because it is in a different location.
If webdev already exists, open that folder and skip creating it. These are new-folder examples; use only the commands for your operating system.
cd C:\

blocks.title: Workspace note
blocks.text: For a new Windows workspace, C:\webdev is one option. On Mac, ~/webdev is a common choice. An existing working course folder can stay where it is; use its actual path. Keep each project in its own subfolder.
claude
blocks.where: Normal terminal · PowerShell or Mac shell
blocks.label: Terminal command
blocks.note: Paste into the named input area. Press Enter to run.

blocks.text: The very first run walks you through these steps:
Workspace access: it asks whether it may read/modify/run the files in the current folder. If it's your safe folder, choose Yes, I trust this folder.
Text style: pick a terminal color theme. You can change it later.
Account: choose Claude account with subscription and log in with your subscription account (the API pay-per-use option makes costs hard to predict — not recommended).
Security note: a warning to always review the results and never blindly run code of unclear origin — this protects you against attacks like prompt injection.
Just type what you want in natural language in the prompt input area (e.g., “Build me a simple personal-intro website”).
For a line break, type \ and then Enter.
Typed the wrong thing? The ESC key cancels what's running.
To quit Claude Code, press Ctrl + C twice.
Change the AI model:  /model
Type /model in the prompt box to pick which model to use:
/model
blocks.label: Claude Code command
blocks.note: Paste into the named input area. Press Enter to run.

blocks.text:
Select Model
    Haiku
  > Sonnet
    Opus
blocks.label: Example output — do not type

blocks.text: Choose a model with the arrow keys and confirm with Enter.
Haiku — light and fast, but less capable.
Sonnet — the best-balanced default on the Pro plan.
Opus — the smartest, but it burns tokens quickly; save it for genuinely hard tasks.
Check token usage:  /usage
Type /usage to see how much you've used:
/usage
blocks.label: Claude Code command
blocks.note: Paste into the named input area. Press Enter to run.

blocks.text:
Claude Usage
  Current Session   42%
  Current Week      18%
blocks.label: Example output — do not type

blocks.text: Current Session — short-term usage that refills every 5 hours.
Current Week — usage accumulated over the week.
If either one gets close to 100%, responses may be limited for a while — glance at this gauge before assigning a big task; it's your budget meter for AI work.

blocks.title: Before you continue
blocks.text: Claude Code input and the normal terminal prompt are different places. Enter /usage inside Claude Code. Enter shell commands such as cd and ls in a normal PowerShell or Mac shell prompt, using another terminal or leaving Claude Code first.
Time to delegate your first real task: a light personal-intro page, requested with a prompt like this:

Request: Build me a simple personal-intro website.
- My name is Alex Carter
- Don't decorate it; keep the code under 200 characters
- When it's done, open it in a web browser
- Save the code as index.html
blocks.label: Claude Code prompt
blocks.note: Paste into Claude Code and press Enter. Review its proposed changes.

blocks.text: Claude Code creates index.html. Review any requested changes, then open the file in a browser if it does not open automatically. Check the name and the simple layout. In the next chapter, you will use VS Code to inspect and edit the file. If VS Code was installed during setup, keep that installation.
